grades.reason: Describes how LoongArch recognizes and responds to interrupts (ESTAT.IS, ECFG.LIE, CRMD.IE). It does not cover a wait-for-interrupt or idle instruction, or what it guarantees about suspension and resumption.

grades.quote: Implementations are permitted to resume execution for any reason, even if an enabled interrupt has not become pending. Hence, a legal implementation is to simply implement the WFI instruction as a NOP.
grades.reason: Directly describes what RISC-V WFI guarantees and does not guarantee about resuming. An enabled interrupt that is or becomes pending resumes the hart, and the trap is taken on the following instruction. The hart may also resume for any reason, so WFI can be a NOP. Software must therefore recheck for pending interrupts and loop. WFI works with interrupts globally disabled, and resumption honors individual local enables.
